title: feat(react-instantsearch): server-side rendering
body:
**Summary** This proposes a simple solution to support server-side rendering. The idea is to remove the need to do async actions from `` when rendering on the server side. Instead, we let the user fetch algolia results themselves, and inject them into `` through a new `resultsState` prop. Links to #1687, #1531, #1869 **Result** Here is a snippet from a server. `index` uses the bestbuy example: ```js function handleRender(req, res) { index.search('').then(state => { const html = renderToStaticMarkup( ) res.send(renderFullPage(html)) }) } ``` The rendered result is: ```html Server-side rendering example

comments.body:
Thanks @mikaa123 for this proposal 👍 

I'm curious but what's behind this: `index.search('')`?
@mthuret just the good old [algoliasearch index search method](https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-client/javascript/search/#search-an-index) :)
@mikaa123 How would you handle facet filters and values?

I think even as a first step we don't want users to do their own mapping between the InstantSearch search state and the helper/client one. 

I think what we need is a way to perform the search before any rendering. 

Also if have a props to set the results state then we need a way to get him back (could be useful for some others use cases). But what I have in mind is more a results state that will be already formatted according to widgets (like the search state). Basically, a way to get back all the provided props of connectors.

> I think what we need is a way to perform the search before any rendering.

That's the theory for being able to create server side rendering. However with react-instantsearch we have a declarative API based on widget configuration. The whole idea is to keep the configuration definition is a single form. Having a way to configure the search before explicitly writing the widgets means to have another way of defining this configuration, right?

You both have good points.
I haven't tried it yet, but what about creating an `InstantSearchManager` (directly from createInstantSearchManager), perform a search on it, and inject it to an InstantSearch widget?

> I haven't tried it yet, but what about creating an InstantSearchManager (directly from createInstantSearchManager), perform a search on it, and inject it to an InstantSearch widget?

That's already the purpose of the JS Helper. I am open to discussion and ideas on how to move forward with the stack but I would prefer not to create yet another abstraction. React-instantsearch is pretty hard to grasp already and I think we should move towards less mechanics than more.

That's my 2cts and I'm open to discussing based on prototypes :)

This is a nice hack that shows we are not that far from being able to do server side rendering.

As already discussed the only drawback is that it relies on client.search() (raw search results) and this would be too complex for users to determine what to do in here.

Asynchronous server side rendering seems to be a common issue, see https://www.google.com/search?q=react+asynchronous+server+side+render maybe there are non-explored gems here.
Thanks for taking the time to dig into this.
